description:
`cleanUrls` with an unparseable glob pattern. The reference's minimatch silently treats unparseable patterns as never-matching and the server keeps running (`serve-handler/src/index.js:38-67` via `minimatch`); other patterns in the list, if any, continue to work. IrServe mirrors this graceful degradation: invalid patterns are skipped with a stderr warning, server starts, and `applicable` returns false for the invalid-only configuration so neither phase 4 (cleanUrls 301) nor phase 8 (extensionless resolution) fires. Backs SRV-ROUT-001's array-form scope. Closes Codex review round 2 P2.

Note: this probe only requests `/page.html` (a path with an extension), not `/`. Under `cleanUrls=false` (or the equivalent invalid-only array), the reference does NOT auto-resolve `<dir>/index.html` for directory requests — `findRelated` is gated on `cleanUrl || rewrittenPath` at `index.js:620`, so a `GET /` falls through to `renderDirectory` which emits an HTML listing instead. That broader directory-listing-vs-index behavior is SRV-DLST-* territory (Stage 6g) and is intentionally outside this probe's contract; we exercise only the path that proves invalid patterns don't crash the server and don't fire the cleanUrls 301.
